+# Priya Shah — Runtime Diagnostics Onboarding Plan
+
+Effective: 2026-07-27  
+Role: Senior Runtime Reliability Engineer  
+Team: Runtime Diagnostics, Reliability Engineering  
+Manager: Runtime Diagnostics Engineering Manager  
+Member branch: `person/priya-shah-capture-20260727`
+
+## Role and operating boundary
+
+Priya will turn runtime degradation and release-safety signals into fast, reproducible, evidence-backed findings, then help promote validated findings into durable controls such as runbooks, alerts, regression tests, release gates, or design constraints. She supports SRE during live incidents and Runtime during deep investigation. SRE retains incident command and immediate mitigation authority; Runtime retains ownership of runtime code and fixes; Runtime Diagnostics owns investigation quality, evidence artifacts, validation discipline, and finding-to-control follow-through. [workspace_38ac45fbb6664b5d678f5410, `/knowledge/teams/runtime-diagnostics/operating-plan.md`; workspace_594675f335939dce30b8f76a, `/knowledge/departments/reliability-engineering/charter.md`]
+
+## First-week access and setup checklist
+
+The manager opens or confirms every request before Day 1 and uses the expedited path for anything that blocks Day-1 work. The canonical targets are one business day for Okta/core SSO and security-training assignment, two business days for GitHub and PagerDuty/Datadog access, three business days for Redwood Console's production-sandbox role, and three to seven business days for a new laptop. [dsid_426645772b534ac4a6af358830cf7982, `/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/company-handbook/04_hiring-and-onboarding/new-hire-orientation-and-tooling-guide-2024.json`]
+
+- [ ] **Identity and endpoint security — Day 1:** laptop and peripherals available or delivery tracked; Okta/core SSO active; corporate email, Slack, distribution lists, and relevant Confluence spaces available; MFA enrolled; VPN, disk encryption, endpoint management, and company password manager verified; security, privacy, and code-of-conduct training assigned. Owners: People Ops, IT, Security.
+- [ ] **Engineering workspace — by business Day 2:** GitHub organization membership and least-privilege access to the onboarding and Runtime Diagnostics repositories; local development environment can clone, build, run a test, and exercise CI; team issue tracker and read access to architecture/design material confirmed. Owners: manager, DevOps/Runtime.
+- [ ] **Diagnostics and incident tools — by business Day 2:** Datadog dashboards/logs and PagerDuty rota visible; Priya can acknowledge a test alert but is not placed in an independent production rotation until shadowing and readiness review are complete. Owners: SRE and Observability.
+- [ ] **Runtime sandbox — by business Day 3:** Redwood Console production-sandbox role available; Priya can view the Teams/runtime dashboards and run a sample staging request. Any cloud, production-console write, deploy, routing, or evidence-store access is requested separately through the approved least-privilege flow. Owners: Platform Operations, Runtime, Security.
+- [ ] **Team knowledge — Day 1–3:** access to the Runtime Diagnostics operating plan, department charter, current roadmap, recent incident reviews, runtime architecture, current runbooks, SLO/error-budget views, and release dashboards.
+- [ ] **Access verification pairing — Day 1–3:** manager or buddy witnesses successful SSO, email/Slack, repository access, staging sample request, Datadog dashboard/log lookup, and PagerDuty test-alert acknowledgement; blockers are recorded with owner and expected completion date.
+- [ ] **Required training — by end of Week 1:** complete Secure SDL/security training and the incident-command, data-handling, evidence-retention, and customer-data privacy read-throughs before any write-level production access. The published onboarding requirement is Secure SDL completion within seven days and MFA before write-level repository access. [dsid_60f6461978c149b597fe8894d9da2bd1, `/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/company-handbook/04_hiring-and-onboarding/cohort-onboarding-and-role-activation-manual-2026.json`]
+
+## First 30 days: outcomes and evidence of readiness
+
+### Days 1–5 — orient, verify, and make one safe contribution
+
+- Complete access verification and record every remaining entitlement gap with owner, least-privilege scope, and target date.
+- Review the Runtime Diagnostics intake, artifact, validation, escalation, and finding-promotion workflow; walk one completed incident from alert through durable control.
+- Complete architecture sessions covering request routing, runtime/model versioning, batching/scheduling, GPU and memory behavior, model loading, KV cache, fallback paths, observability, and regional capacity.
+- Shadow an SRE incident/on-call workflow and a Runtime/release workflow; document the difference between SRE command, Runtime implementation ownership, and Diagnostics evidence ownership.
+- Land a small, low-risk contribution of no more than roughly one workday—for example, a runbook clarification, diagnostic query improvement, missing dashboard link, or test fixture—using normal review.
+
+### Days 6–15 — perform supervised diagnosis
+
+- Serve as diagnostics lead or co-lead on one bounded staging exercise, game day, release-gate investigation, or recent-incident replay.
+- Produce a complete case bundle: intake, timeline, environment/config and recent-deploy context, metrics snapshots, minimal traces/logs, hypothesis matrix, probe manifest/results, mitigation record, and validation conclusion.
+- Demonstrate safe evidence handling: hash tenant identifiers and exclude raw prompts or PII unless an approved evidence process requires them.
+- Present the investigation at the weekly Runtime + SRE finding review, clearly separating observation, hypothesis, validation status, residual risk, and next discriminating test.
+- Shadow at least one staged rollout and explain its preflight evidence, canary cohorts, telemetry gates, stop/rollback conditions, decision audit trail, and post-rollback checks.
+
+### Days 16–30 — own a scoped finding-to-control loop
+
+- Lead one scoped diagnostic investigation with a named SRE IC/service owner and Runtime owner. For live work, attach to the incident record and communicate through the IC rather than creating a competing command channel.
+- Reach an explicit conclusion of **validated**, **probable**, or **unresolved** using supporting and contradicting evidence. Do not represent a probable or unresolved hypothesis as fact.
+- For a validated material mechanism or release gap, open at least one durable-control item—a runbook/diagnostic, alert, regression test, release/SLO/compatibility/rollback gate, or design constraint—with owner, due/review date, verification method, and a link to case evidence.
+- Independently review one runtime release evidence packet and state a go/hold/rollback recommendation. Preserve traffic stages, signal deltas, gate decisions, stop/rollback conditions, and the stable observation window; a failed critical gate means stop or rollback, not weakening the gate during the event.
+- Deliver a short knowledge share on the case, the reusable diagnostic technique, and any observability or release-safety gap found.
+- At the Day-30 review, agree the next 60-day ownership area and readiness path for production on-call participation. Readiness is based on demonstrated command-boundary discipline, safe evidence collection, correct escalation, and release-gate judgment—not elapsed time alone.
+
+## Initial debugging responsibilities
+
+1. **Start from the decision and blast radius.** Capture case/incident/change IDs; severity and customer impact; affected tenant cohort, tier, route, model/runtime version, region, and time window; expected versus observed behavior; and the decision the investigation must unblock.
+2. **Preserve context before changing it.** Record recent deploys and configuration changes, feature flags, node/GPU pool and capacity state, rollback/fallback state, and a UTC timeline. Take minimal, policy-compliant snapshots before a mitigation destroys evidence.
+3. **Build a cross-signal picture.** Review p50/p95/p99 latency, 5xx and 429 counts, queue depth/time, CPU/GPU utilization and memory pressure, KV-cache behavior, throughput/token-generation signals, affected routes/models/regions, representative trace IDs, and bounded log slices. [dsid_8cff0d2004fc4c58b2391a0e3cc71556, `/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/observer-lifecycle-and-incident-runloop-for-llm-serving-2026.json`]
+4. **Rank hypotheses and run discriminating probes.** Record evidence for and against each hypothesis, compare against a known-good baseline, change one variable at a time where possible, and make probe commands/parameters reproducible.
+5. **Support incident command; do not supplant it.** Acknowledge through the IC, keep the incident timeline current, and immediately escalate worsening impact, blast-radius growth, multi-region symptoms, a harmful mitigation, exhausted rollback, or an SLO/release-gate crossing. SRE chooses live mitigation. The documented ownership ladder has the pager recipient triage first, an IC established in the 10–30 minute window, and service/engineering ownership joining by 30–90 minutes. [dsid_363b6658e9524c3cbadeb4579d4ac7e0, `/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbook-curation-and-incident-ownership-guidelines-2025.json`]
+6. **Escalate by mechanism.** Runtime/on-call for crash/OOM, kernel/compiler/tokenization, batching/scheduling, model-load, KV-cache, output-integrity, or compatibility; Routing/Fleet/Platform for traffic, failover, quota, GPU pool, control plane, or regional health; Observability for missing or untrustworthy signals; Security/Privacy for sensitive data, residency, audit, or forensic-preservation risk.
+7. **Close the loop.** Capture the final impact and recovery evidence, label the conclusion's confidence, assign corrective actions, and help draft P1/P2 postmortem evidence within 72 hours of stabilization. [dsid_8cff0d2004fc4c58b2391a0e3cc71556, `/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/observer-lifecycle-and-incident-runloop-for-llm-serving-2026.json`]
+
+## Runtime release-safety expectations
+
+- No promotion without preflight checks, green staging/synthetic coverage, working dashboards and alerts, a named release owner and SRE/on-call coverage, a tested rollback path, and explicit gate/abort criteria.
+- Use cohort canaries and staged traffic ramps. Validate latency, error, saturation/resource pressure, correctness/quality, routing, and customer-impact signals against baseline at every stage.
+- Treat missing or unknown required metrics as a blocking gate. Do not promote during an incident or high error-budget burn.
+- Preserve an auditable evidence packet: artifact/version, traffic stages and dwell windows, dashboard and trace links, gate decisions and deltas, operator decisions, rollback/hold actions, and post-release verification.
+- A critical gate failure pauses or rolls back. Validate that latency, error, and saturation return to baseline after rollback and retain evidence of any manual action. The dedicated staged-rollout checklist requires testing promote, abort, hold/resume, and missing-metric behavior; its rollback plan is expected to be executable in under 15 minutes. [dsid_62bd575d44e5409abddcf9836f6f8f6a, `/knowledge/company/sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/release-engineering/launch-checklist-dedicated-staged-rollouts.json`]
+- Reliability Engineering may pause a planned promotion when a defined gate fails; SRE retains emergency mitigation authority, and Runtime retains implementation decisions. [workspace_594675f335939dce30b8f76a, `/knowledge/departments/reliability-engineering/charter.md`]
+
+## Mentors and operating interfaces
+
+- **Engineering manager — outcomes and scope:** weekly 1:1; owns success criteria, access escalation, workload, Day-15 and Day-30 calibration, and selection of the first scoped case.
+- **Primary technical mentor — Runtime/serving lead:** twice-weekly for the first month; covers architecture, code paths, performance/compatibility mechanisms, reproducible experiments, and review of the first diagnostic case.
+- **Incident mentor — SRE/on-call lead:** weekly plus shadow shifts; covers severity, pager/bridge mechanics, IC boundary, mitigation handoff, timeline quality, and readiness for future rotation participation.
+- **Technical buddy — Runtime Diagnostics engineer:** daily check-ins in Week 1, then twice weekly; helps with local setup, evidence-bundle mechanics, current cases, and first contribution review.
+- **Observability liaison:** dashboards, alert semantics, trace/log access, signal quality, telemetry cardinality, and evidence retention.
+- **Release Engineering liaison:** release evidence packets, cohort canaries, gate evaluation, rollback drills, and audit trail.
+- **Routing/Fleet/Platform interfaces:** failover, traffic policy, regional capacity, GPU pools, quotas, control plane, and service-specific entitlements.
+- **Security/Privacy and People Ops/IT:** least-privilege approval, customer-data handling, forensic preservation, device/account provisioning, required training, and SLA escalation.
+- **Review cadence:** daily active-case/evidence check with the team as needed; weekly Runtime + SRE finding review; Day-15 and Day-30 manager/mentor reviews.
+
+## Evidence register
+
+- `workspace_38ac45fbb6664b5d678f5410` — `/knowledge/teams/runtime-diagnostics/operating-plan.md` — active team purpose, boundaries, intake, required artifacts, validation states, escalation, durable-control promotion, and review cadence.
+- `workspace_594675f335939dce30b8f76a` — `/knowledge/departments/reliability-engineering/charter.md` — department mission, SRE/Runtime boundaries, SLO-gated reversible release policy, interfaces, and decision rights.
+- `dsid_426645772b534ac4a6af358830cf7982` — `/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/company-handbook/04_hiring-and-onboarding/new-hire-orientation-and-tooling-guide-2024.json` — canonical access SLAs, Day 0–1 setup, and access-verification checks.
+- `dsid_60f6461978c149b597fe8894d9da2bd1` — `/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/company-handbook/04_hiring-and-onboarding/cohort-onboarding-and-role-activation-manual-2026.json` — standardized engineering access defaults, baseline provisioning target, Secure SDL timing, and MFA requirement.
+- `dsid_363b6658e9524c3cbadeb4579d4ac7e0` — `/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbook-curation-and-incident-ownership-guidelines-2025.json` — incident ownership ladder, first-responder/IC/service-owner timing, diagnostic runbook requirements, and escalation.
+- `dsid_8cff0d2004fc4c58b2391a0e3cc71556` — `/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/observer-lifecycle-and-incident-runloop-for-llm-serving-2026.json` — runtime incident metrics and P1/P2 postmortem timing.
+- `dsid_62bd575d44e5409abddcf9836f6f8f6a` — `/knowledge/company/sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/release-engineering/launch-checklist-dedicated-staged-rollouts.json` — staged rollout, required gate behavior, rollback triggers, sub-15-minute rollback expectation, and post-rollback validation.
*** End Patch
